chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala ibn Ayub from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and his son Ismail was with him. He said, 'What prevents Ibn Abi Sammak from sending out the youth of the Shi'a, so that they suffice him as the people suffice him, and give them what the people give?' Then he said to me, 'Why did you leave your stipend?' I said, 'Out of fear for my religion.' He said, 'What prevented Ibn Abi Sammak from sending your stipend to you? Did he not know that you have a share in the treasury (Bayt al-Mal)?'

key_terms.ابْنُ أَبِي سَمَّاكٍ: Ibn Abi Sammak, the administrator of funds

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on receiving stipends from the public treasury for the Shi'a according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Imam’s emphasis on the institutional right of the Shi'a to public stipends (*ata'*) from the *Bayt al-Mal*, countering the tendency of believers to withhold their share due to fear of political persecution (*khawf*). It underscores the principle that financial sustenance is a divine right tied to one's status, encouraging the community to claim their due without compromising their faith. The narrative serves as a practical guide for managing economic independence within the framework of Shia governance.
